reading_text: You are down on the floor, watching a child let go of the chair and cross open space on unsteady legs. This is Berkana, Anna, the moment a thing that grew unseen for months takes its first step into the room. You stand at the edge of the floor, where the ground holds firm under your feet.

The fog sits thick on the water, hiding the far shore, the boats, everything but the few feet of dark waves at your side. Then even those fade, and only the sound of the tide against stone remains. This is Blank, the not-yet-seen, and it speaks in its own time.

The door stands open, and coffee waits on the table for two, still steaming. This is Gebo, the warmth that only wakes when it passes between people. Whatever you choose ahead, some of it will only come to you through another hand meeting yours. The second cup is poured, and it holds its heat while you decide.

The line where the turf meets the ground is the part you would walk past, Anna, yet it is where the wall first takes hold. From there it rises and turns the wind, so the doorway between the two paths stays calm. Algiz is that steady edge that lets you stand where the ways divide without being pushed. When you look down each track, which one carries you and which one only pulls?

The green comes up over the bed while the earth beneath it still holds the seed unseen. This is Ingwaz, Anna, the slow work that shows in the grass before it shows on the surface. What has passed between two paths was already deciding itself long before either way was clear. Which of the two roots you first, or neither yet?

The phone rings, and the voice says the thing you have waited to hear, and for a moment two roads stand open before you. Ansuz is the word that travels across air to reach an ear that was ready for it. Now the waiting has ended and the choosing has not yet begun. The light is already turning grey toward morning.

Two cups sit on the table between you and someone, one already cold, the steam gone from the other. Isa is that stillness where nothing moves toward and nothing moves away. The waiting holds its own weight, and it does not thaw because you wish it to.

You are walking a level track, Anna, and the one beside you matches your step without a word between you. Ehwaz is that quiet agreement of two who move as one, neither pulling ahead nor falling back. The pace holds only while both keep choosing it, stride for stride. You are on the path now, walking alongside another.

Under the low green leaves the fruit is already forming, small and pale, weeks yet from the dark ripeness August brings. Fehu is the slow filling of what two hands have tended together, before either can taste it. What grows between people is like this, gathered in a season that will not be hurried. You are standing on the heath while it is still ripening.

Where the shadow ends the light begins, and the valley holds its breath as the sun comes over the ridge. This is Wunjo, Anna, the ease that settles when two people stop pushing against each other. What was cold in the morning is warm now, and nothing is asking to be decided in a hurry. You stand in that first still light, watching what wants to grow.

At the hour the sun should sink, it only leans low along the ridge and rises again without ever going dark. This is Sowilo, Anna, the light that stayed through what you thought was an ending between you and someone. Look back and see the warmth never fully left the room. You are standing in a season where the sun did not set.

You stand in the ruined farmstead, walls broken but the hearthstones still warm under your hand. Othila is the warmth a place keeps long after the fire has gone. Morning light finds you here, Anna, where the doorway still opens outward.

Look at the single hoofprint pressed into the turf, the one no eye lingers on. From these small marks the whole sheep-track finds its way along the hillside, and that is what Raidho does — it lets a path form step by step, not by plan. The route behind you was never drawn before you walked it. When you follow the ground rather than the map, does that steady you or does it wear you thin?

You stand at the edge of the hayfield, the grass cut to green stubble and the mown rows lying open to the sun, not yet dry enough to gather. Jera is that waiting the field keeps between cutting and carrying, unhurried by any hand. You are standing among people who know the crop comes in when it is ready, not before.

The face in the rain-barrel holds still while the water trembles at its edge, and it is yours, older than you remember. Mannaz is that seeing yourself plainly across the work you have done. Every choice you made about what to keep and what to abandon rose from that same face. What you gave to the making, Anna, it gave back to you.

Where the black lava meets the green, the rock still holds the heat that shaped it under moss grown slow and cool. This is Uruz, the old fire settling into ground you can walk on. As you find your footing here, what will you shelter and what will you leave open?
